title: Private deploy quickstart + onboarding idea pad
content:
[scratchpad — informal]

Goal: reduce time-to-first-success for a Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) from days to <2 hours for an engineer-proof-of-concept. Focus: guided checks, sane defaults, telemetry opt-in, sample workload, and rollback safety.

Why: customers keep getting stuck on basic networking permissions, KMS, and model pin mismatch. Sales + SEs spend ~6–12hrs per evaluation on repetitive triage.

Top-level ideas (brain dump):
- Guided onboarding wizard (CLI + Console) that runs preflight checks in order and reports fixes with copy-paste commands. Keep it idempotent.
- "Lightweight demo stack": single-node docker compose / k8s manifest that runs inference with a tiny model and synthetic traffic generator. Purpose: validate runtime, routing, and billing hooks without full infra.
- Prebundled sample prompts & eval set: a 20-prompt suite that exercises streaming, function-calling, and embeddings. Runs automatically to surface regressions.
- Telemetry & logs opt-in step: explain what we collect (latency quantiles, token counts, error traces) and provide toggle + retention option.
- Default security pattern: suggest KMS key path, default IAM roles, and a minimal firewall rule set (CIDR templates).
- Quantization & perf preset: pick "dev-fast" profile that uses int8 CPU fallback or small-quant model to reduce GPU reqs.
- Rollback plan + safe defaults: set canary split, autoscale min replicas=1, max=3, and an emergency abort command.

User stories (rough):
- As an SRE trying out Redwood Private, I want a one-click preflight so I can know network & KMS issues before deploying, -> acceptance: preflight returns pass/fail with remediation commands.
- As a solutions engineer, I want a single-node demo stack to share with a customer so they can validate end-to-end without full infra, -> acceptance: demo stack serves sample responses over local port and reports token usage.
- As a platform engineer, I want the onboarding wizard to produce a git-ready manifest (k8s/terraform snippets) so I can incorporate into infra-as-code.
- As an engineering manager, I want telemetry opt-in explained in plain language so legal/security can sign off faster.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console flow: "Start private quickstart" that runs preflight checks and shows 1-click fixes for the top 6 failure modes.
- CLI equivalent: redwood private quickstart --email <se> generates the same artifact and a zip with logs + manifest.
- Demo stack: docker-compose.yml that boots the runtime + small model and a generator; returns a hello-style inference JSON.
- Sample prompts run and produce a pass/fail matrix (latency < 200ms p50 for local test, correctness check via fuzzy match).
- Telemetry toggle saved to customer config and a short policy doc emitted in the zip.

Metrics to validate success (for first 90 days):
- Reduction in SE triage time from median 8hrs -> <2hrs for PoC installs.
- % of Private signups that reach first successful inference within 48hrs (goal 60%).
- Opt-in telemetry rate (target 75% of trials).
- Number of follow-on Dedicated conversions from quickstart trials.

Open questions / unknowns (todo list):
- How to safely include KMS/HSM examples without leaking secrets? Can we provide a dummy KMS provider shim for PoC?
- Licensing concerns for packaging small open models in the demo stack — need legal check.
- Which tiny model to pick? opt: llama-mini-3b-quant or distilled-flan? Perf vs license tradeoffs.
- Multi-region network check: how deep should we go on validating egress rules for enterprise networks? Keep it minimal for MVP.
- Should we support air-gapped installs with offline artifact bundles in MVP or postpone?

UX sketch (console text flow):
1) "Start Private Quickstart" button -> modal: select environment (local/k8s/vpc) -> enter contact email for bundle
2) Run preflight (30–90s) with progress bar; items: DNS resolvability, KMS handshake, ports, CPU/GPU availability, disk space, firewall rules, docker/k8s versions
3) Results: green/yellow/red badges with "Fix" pill that expands remediation steps and copy-button commands
4) If green: show "Launch demo stack" (1 click) -> status logs -> sample inference URL + artifacts.zip download
5) Telemetry modal: checkbox + short bullets "we collect X, Y, Z" and link to retention policy; default: on for 30 days

CLI sketch:
- redwood private quickstart --env k8s --email se@example.com --no-telemetry
- prints preflight failures with remediation steps, writes artifacts to ./redwood-quickstart-<ts>/

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: demo stack gives false confidence (works locally but fails at scale). Mitigation: clear messaging "PoC only — not production" and link to Dedicated capacity guide.
- Risk: telemetry opt-out reduces our ability to triage. Mitigation: include a compact local diagnostic bundle that customers can upload to support.
- Risk: shipping model weights triggers license & download friction. Mitigation: default to a public small model or provide instructions to pull model from customer's approved bucket.

Implementation notes (engineering):
- Small product team: 1 PM (me), 1 UX, 2 engineers (1 infra, 1 runtime), 1 SE rotational for week 1 testing.
- Delivery: 6-week sprint for MVP (preflight + demo stack + CLI).
- Quick wins: implement preflight checks (network, docker/k8s version, CPU/GPU presence) and produce a zip with diagnostics.
- Medium work: demo stack + sample prompts + fuzzy-check runner.

Next steps (action items):
- [ ] Sync with Legal about model bundling options (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Prototype preflight checks in a single script and test against three customer networks (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Wire console modal mockups (owner: UX)
- [ ] Draft support playbook for SEs to escalate if quickstart fails (owner: Kai)

Notes to self: keep language non-promising to customers "quickstart for evaluation" not "production install". Capture common failure snippets and include copy-paste fixes (eg iptables rules, KMS permission JSON).

Random partial log from spike run 2024-09-30:
- Preflight: DNS ok, docker 24.0, kernel mismatch warning on ubuntu-20.04, KMS handshake timed out (fix: open outbound 443 to kms.example.com), demo stack launched but model failed to load (403 on download — need auth token guidance).

End of pad.

(If this grows too long move into PD Confluence page and track as JIRA epic.)
